description: A Cortex-Harness configuration file: the user's `config.toml`, a project's `.cortex/config.toml` or `.cortex/config.local.toml`, or the managed file. Generated from the settings in `crates/cortex-config`; not edited by hand. `x-cortex-trust` says what a project's file may set, and `x-cortex-effect` when a change takes effect.

adapt.description: Variant overrides per model, and the map and profile budgets.

compat.description: Which files written for other tools are read.

mcp.description: MCP server definitions of other clients, offered for import.

config_version.description: The version of the configuration schema the file was written for. A file with a newer version than this build understands is refused.

context.description: The compaction trigger and settings, and instruction file names.

credentials.description: Where stored credentials are kept. Never the credentials themselves: no key of this file takes a secret.

store.description: The store for API keys saved with `cortex auth login`.

http.description: The HTTP client: the connect timeout, a proxy, and extra certificate authorities.

limits.description: The most a turn, a session and a day may spend.

day.description: Limits on one day, across sessions.

cost.x-cortex-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a higher one user only

requests.x-cortex-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a higher one user only

time.x-cortex-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a higher one user only

tokens.x-cortex-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a higher one user only

tokens.x-cortex-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a higher one user only

level.description: The level (`error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug` or `trace`), optionally followed by levels for target prefixes: `"info,cortex_llm=debug"`. The `CORTEX_LOG` variable and `--log-level` override it.

managed.description: For the managed file of a shared machine only.

locked.description: Keys that no layer above the managed file may change. A table's name locks every key in it. Read from the managed file only.

mcp.description: MCP servers by name, and MCP settings.

model.description: Models by role, the reasoning level and the speed tier.

effort.description: The reasoning level of the main role: one of the model's own levels, or `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high` or `max`.

fast.description: The model for utility calls: summaries, titles. Without one, the main model is used.

judge.description: The model for model-graded comparisons. Without one, the main model is used.

main.description: The model for the agent's own turns. Needed to run a turn.

max_output.description: The most output tokens one response may have. Without it, the model's own limit applies.

reasoning.description: How much of the model's reasoning is shown.

effort.description: The role's reasoning level. For `main` it overrides `model.effort`.

provider.description: The provider that serves the role's model. Needed only when two providers have a model with the same name.

speed.description: The role's speed tier. For `main` it overrides `model.speed`.

The session's speed tier, which the main role runs at: `standard`, `fast` where the model offers it, or a provider's own tier name. The utility roles do not follow it: they run at `standard` unless `model.roles.<role>.speed` says otherwise.

speed_cooldown.description: How long requests stay at `standard` after a fallback, when the provider does not say when the tier is available again.

speed_fallback.description: Whether a request that a speed tier refuses is sent again at `standard`. When off, such a refusal is an ordinary rate limit.

speed_wait.description: The longest one request waits in place for a speed tier before it falls back to `standard`. `"0s"` never waits.

models.description: Catalog overrides and additions by model name: limits, prices, reasoning control, capability flags.

permissions.description: The permission mode and the permission rules.

mode.description: The session's level: how much runs without asking.
mode.x-cortex-trust: by level: not above the mode in effect is a preference, up to `supervised` widens access, above it user only

rules.description: Permission rules. Every layer adds to the list; `deny` beats `ask` beats `allow`, whatever the order.
rules.x-cortex-trust: by action: `deny` and `ask` are preferences, `allow` widens access

profile.description: The profile to apply: the name of a `[profiles.<name>]` table. The `--profile` flag overrides it. A project's file may define profiles and may not select one: a profile the user wrote is applied with the user's rights, so a repository that could pick it could switch on whatever the user's loosest profile allows.

profiles.description: Named sets of settings. A profile may hold any key of this file except `profile`, `profiles`, `managed` and `config_version`.

enabled.description: Whether the provider is available. `false` removes an entry that a lower layer or the built-in table defines.

first_event_timeout.description: How long to wait for the first event of a response. Overrides `retry.first_event_timeout` for this provider.

headers.description: Extra headers for every request. A value is text, or `{ env = "NAME" }` to read an environment variable when used.

idle_timeout.description: How long a response stream may be silent before the request fails. Overrides `retry.idle_timeout` for this provider.

key_env.description: The environment variable that holds the provider's API key. It is looked at before the credential store.

protocol.description: The wire protocol the endpoint speaks.

providers.description: Providers by name. A built-in provider needs no entry; an entry changes it or adds a new one. `enabled = false` removes one.

retry.description: How a request that failed is tried again.

attempts.description: The most attempts for one request, the first included.

backoff_base.description: The wait before the second attempt. Each later wait is this multiplied by `backoff_factor` again, up to `backoff_cap`.

backoff_cap.description: The longest wait between two attempts.

backoff_factor.description: What the wait is multiplied by after each attempt.

first_event_timeout.description: How long to wait for the first event of a response.

idle_timeout.description: How long a response stream may be silent before the request fails.

max_wait.description: The longest wait a provider may ask for. A longer one ends the turn with the error and the provider's hint.

rpc.description: The RPC server: socket path, token, client timeouts.

runs.description: The run engine: concurrency, workspaces, budgets.

sandbox.description: What a command the harness starts may touch.

enabled.description: Whether commands are confined by the OS sandbox where there is one.

network.description: Whether a command may use the network.
network.x-cortex-trust: by value: `off` is a preference, `full` widens access

protect.description: Paths a command may not change, besides the built-in ones. Every layer adds to the list.

write.description: Paths a command may write besides the workspace. Every layer adds to the list.

data_dir.description: The data directory. A leading `~` is the home directory. Without it the platform's usual place is used.

shell.description: The shell that runs commands: program, arguments, time limits.

stats.description: Whether local statistics are recorded, and for how long.

tools.description: Enabled tools, output limits and per-tool settings.

tui.description: The terminal UI: presenter, theme, density.

usage.description: The usage view: week start, ranges, the opt-in refresh and the other tools whose records may be read.

verify.description: The verification mode, commands and time limits.
